what: ARMS-r3 section 7 (P4) Viterbi pack decision: quality first (paired tests over the fixed eval items, greedy self-consistency control), then speed (ARMS.md step 6 noise rule) on the four counted boots CUR-1, VIT-1, CUR-2, VIT-2 (results/2026-09-26-serve-r3/). Computed by decision-viterbi-compute.py.txt from the raw per-boot files (lail10.txt, bench_decode.txt, four/four_numbers.json, four/02-micro.log, four/06-prose-long.log, quality_{quick,full}.json, gate files) through the same per-boot readers as decision-bundle-compute.py.txt; stdlib statistics only.

inputs.image: dsv41-flash-exl3-sm121:review-e14 = sha256:3a002b55c9bc... on both ranks, every boot
inputs.config: the promoted config on every boot: round-34 defaults + the 10 K envs (DSV41_P2B_COOP=2 ... DSV41_INDEXER_WP_GEMV=1); KP add-ons off; AUDIT=strict
inputs.order: CUR-1, VIT-1, CUR-2, VIT-2 (s7 order), each the first attempt, no fix or retry
inputs.code_between_boots: git diff --stat 7db92e93a10c..ebeec5ed1962 outside results/: empty (only evidence and the viterbi-precheck results were committed between boots)
inputs.docker_patch: sha256 list digest adaaac7a0f40a2a1 on all four boots (61 files)
inputs.snapshots_loaded: quality provenance root and four/serve_cmd.json name the intended snapshot on every boot; boot.txt shows only that snapshot
inputs.viterbi_kernel_precheck: results/2026-09-25-kernels/integration/viterbi-precheck (commit 8bf97c5): l20 --ref and l33 tp-rank 1, 24/24 checks each, pass

sources: stage task: promote only if quality is better or equal on every gate with at least one significant improvement (NLL expected) and speed is not worse beyond noise; else reject
quality: quick AND full pass on both VIT boots, no component outside its band (s7); quick must pass on every candidate boot (ARMS.md step 6)
every gate better or equal vs CUR (paired where the data allow: NLL per passage, GSM8K/MMLU/tools/needle per item)
at least one significant improvement (NLL expected)
speed: primary: ms/step at matched acceptance (per-boot median_run_acceptance_len intervals overlap); if not matched, the arm changed drafting and the gate is tok/s with the same noise rule
s7: gate on prose_long c=1 tok/s and L.A.I.L tok/s with the noise rule; ms/step at matched kernels should be equal within noise
noise = larger boot-to-boot spread (max-min of per-boot values) of the two arms; 'worse beyond noise' = VIT median below the CUR median by more than the noise
non-inferiority: pp_warm/pp_novel 8k/32k, prose_long c=2 aggregate, warm-prefix not worse by more than the noise

notes: No boot is VOID: gpu_guard --check rc=0 (0 FOREIGN) on all four; no CONTAMINATED marker; disarm_scan rc 0; strict audit ok with COOP=2 and lm_head mxfp8 engaged once per rank on every boot (engagement.txt).
CUR-1 e2e rc was not captured directly (e2e.py ran in the background); e2e.txt records pass_rate 3/3, and main() returns 0 only when every phase passes.
VIT-2: the guards started after run.sh exited and before the smokes; nothing was measured in between.
Slow L.A.I.L runs inside clean boots were kept as measured (CUR-1 runs 4/5/10, CUR-2 run 3, VIT-2 runs 5/8); the per-boot medians are the gate values.

VIT-1 side reading, not scored: the main checkout's smoke_vision.py (1x1 'red' JPEG, pass rule = no HTTP 400) answered 'Gray' 3/3 on VIT-1. No CUR reading of that image exists, so it cannot be paired. The 64x64 red PNG reads 'Red' on all 8 CUR/VIT quality readings and in every worktree smoke.

nll.unit: per-passage mean NLL (nats/token), 40 fixed passages; arm value per passage = mean of its 4 readings (quick + full first pass, 2 boots)

checkable_answers_in_greedy_text.note: Decoded offline from token ids with tokenizer.json (byte-level BPE). Readings: baseline 2 modes x 2 runs; each arm 2 boots x 2 modes x 2 runs. Prompts 0 (17*19), 8 (quadratic) and 11 (IEEE 754) are cut by the 128-token cap before their final answer in every reading of every arm, the 09-24 baseline included, so they are not scored.

decision.verdict: REJECT SNAPSHOT_SHA=2.0bpw-mcg-viterbi-lmhead-mxfp8. Two independent grounds, each sufficient under the rule as written. (1) Quality: quick and full FAIL on both VIT boots, on selfcons.golden_hazard only (ARMS.md step 6 needs quick to pass on every candidate boot; ARMS-r3 s7 needs quick and full to pass with no component outside its band), so 'better or equal on every gate' does not hold even though NLL improves far beyond its CI. (2) Speed: acceptance is not matched, so the s7 gate is tok/s on the honest cells with the noise rule; L.A.I.L tok/s is worse beyond the noise (-1.024 tok/s, -2.38%, noise 0.345; both VIT boots below the CUR median), while prose_long c=1 tok/s is better beyond it (+3.108, +7.04%, noise 2.754). The serve pin stays SNAPSHOT_SHA=2.0bpw-mcg-lmhead-mxfp8.

summary_numbers.ms_step_c1: four prose -0.084 (noise 0.185), prose_long -0.032 (noise 0.426), L.A.I.L -0.322 (noise 0.733) ms/step: equal within noise, as s7 expects

reading: Quality apart from the golden gate is equal or better on every component. NLL drops by 42.12% per passage on average (39/40 passages lower); the one passage that rises (pg98-0, +0.01679) is comparable to the largest same-arm cross-boot per-passage deltas (max |delta| 0.01407-0.02766). MMLU (+10/+6 items per pair), GSM8K (+2/+3), tools exact_args (+1/+0/+2/+1 per reading pair) all move toward VIT, but none of them is significant after pooling the two pairs (sign tests p 0.1338, 0.21875, 0.5). GSM8K-think, needle, json_valid, no_call, c2 and vision are identical.

The golden gate compares greedy text with the 09-24 baseline, which ran the old pack (canonical-e12, 2.0bpw-mcg-lmhead-mxfp8). 8 of 12 prompts diverge from it at the identical token on all 16 VIT sequences (first_div [0, 1, 5, 7]); prompts [3, 5] never diverge; prompts [1, 9] diverge at varying tokens ({1: [1, 9], 9: [3, 20]}). VIT diverges from CUR's own run A in the same way (0.09756-0.10204 quick). Against itself VIT is as stable as CUR: cross-boot hazard VIT-2 vs VIT-1 0.01341 quick / 0.00985 full, CUR-2 vs CUR-1 0.01825 / 0.01675. The decoded VIT texts are coherent and differ in wording and format from token 0; answers that fit in 128 tokens: first 20 primes: baseline 4/4, CUR 8/8, VIT 8/8; French: renard + chien: baseline 4/4, CUR 8/8, VIT 8/8; capital of Australia -> Canberra: baseline 4/4, CUR 8/8, VIT 8/8. So the gate fails because the pack is different, not because the output is unstable. The rule as written does not exempt a pack change; changing that is for the protocol owner.

Speed moves only through acceptance: c=1 ms/step is equal within the noise on every c=1 cell. Acceptance moved in opposite directions by prompt: prose_long c=1 up (run-level MWU p 0.01676), L.A.I.L down (p 0.03593), short prose down (a cell that is 57-64% post-EOS text), structured at 4.0 on every VIT run. At run level (pooled, not the gate) the L.A.I.L tok/s drop has MWU p 0.18058 (Hodges-Lehmann -0.7857 tok/s) and the prose_long gain p 0.00911 (HL +3.06). The L.A.I.L 3x after c=2 cell reads [41.17, 43.66] vs [42.26, 43.09] (inside its noise 2.49). The net speed effect on a mixed workload is not settled by two prompts.

structured c=2 is -5.38 ms/step (+13.01% aggregate), beyond its noise 0.2. On both CUR boots the two c=2 streams start staggered (median TTFT gap 0.233/0.228 s); on both VIT boots they start together (gap 0.0/0.0 s) and, at acceptance 4.0, run in lockstep (equal per-stream ms/step on 8/9 and 9/9 runs). Prose c=2 shows the same start pattern (gap 0.253/0.255 vs 0.001/0.0 s) with ms/step unchanged. Structured c=1 TTFT is 0.209/0.21 s on VIT vs 0.177/0.177 s on CUR. This is a request-admission/batch-phase difference, not a decode kernel change; its cause is not established (s7: 'a ms/step change means something else moved').
structured c=1 ms/step reads +0.321 against a noise of 0.321 (at the noise edge; tok/s +0.257, inside its noise). It is not a gate metric.

open_items: For the protocol owner: selfcons.golden_hazard compares with the old pack's greedy text, so a pack change fails it by construction. If pack changes are to be judged on NLL, task scores and VIT's own A/A plus cross-boot hazard (all equal or better here), the rule has to change first. That change does not happen in this decision.

Even with that change, s7's speed gate needs L.A.I.L tok/s not worse beyond noise. Acceptance moved in opposite directions by prompt (prose_long up, L.A.I.L down). With n=2 boots per arm the noise is one range per arm (L.A.I.L CUR 0.195, VIT 0.345), and the pooled run-level test (not the gate) gives p 0.18058 for L.A.I.L tok/s. A broader prompt set for acceptance, or more CUR/VIT boots, would settle the net speed effect.
The structured and prose c=2 start pattern (staggered on CUR, together on VIT) and the +0.03 s structured c=1 TTFT on VIT are unexplained.
If the pack is reconsidered: a paired CUR/VIT reading of the main-checkout 1x1 JPEG smoke (VIT-1 answered 'Gray') would show whether that answer depends on the pack.
